title: One Year After Gaza Ceasefire: Trump's Board of Peace Has Achieved Little, Progress Stalled
detail: One year after the US-brokered ceasefire was supposed to end the Israel-Hamas war, analysis from Al Jazeera and AP finds that Trump's Board of Peace has achieved limited results. Key outstanding issues remain unresolved, with diplomatic progress largely stalled. The anniversary marks a year since the ceasefire deal took effect, but negotiations toward a permanent settlement have made minimal headway.

media.caption: One year after the Gaza ceasefire deal, diplomatic progress under Trump's Board of Peace has largely stalled

title: Former Biden Official Accuses Netanyahu of Deliberately Delaying Gaza Ceasefire by Six Months for Political Reasons
detail: A former Biden administration official has accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of deliberately delaying a Gaza ceasefire deal by approximately six months for domestic political reasons. The accusation suggests Netanyahu's political calculus — specifically his coalition government's survival and electoral pressures — drove prolonged negotiations that could have concluded sooner. The charge echoes earlier criticisms noting that Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners, including Finance Minister Smotrich and National Security Minister Ben Gvir, consistently opposed any deal that would end the war.

title: Israeli Forces Destroy Building in Gaza One Year Into Ceasefire Agreement
detail: Israeli forces destroyed a building in Gaza on October 10, 2026, one year after the ceasefire agreement was reached. The attack underscores the continued fragility of the truce, with Israel maintaining military operations inside the territory despite the formal ceasefire framework. The strike comes as international attention focuses on the anniversary of the ceasefire deal and the lack of substantive progress toward a permanent resolution.

media.caption: Israeli attack destroys a building in Gaza one year into the ceasefire agreement

title: Former Shin Bet Official: Hamas Retains Full Control of Gaza, Generates Up to $5 Million Per Day in Revenue
detail: A former official from Shin Bet (Israel's internal security service) stated that Hamas retains full control of Gaza one year into the ceasefire and generates up to $5 million per day in revenue. The assessment highlights Hamas's sustained administrative and economic grip on the territory despite the ceasefire, with the group leveraging taxation, border fees, and other mechanisms to fund its operations. The revelation raises questions about the effectiveness of the ceasefire in weakening Hamas's governance capacity.
